key_insight: Sb doping creates bright, self-trapped exciton emission in Cs2BInCl6 nanocrystals, while Na-to-K alloying tunes the exciton lattice distortion and shifts photoluminescence energy without strongly changing absorption.
engineering_relevance: These lead-free double perovskites offer composition-tunable optical fingerprints for safer optoelectronic materials, with polarization-resolved emission providing a practical handle to probe and optimize excitonic behavior.
method: Optical spectroscopy of Sb-doped Cs2BInCl6 nanocrystals across B-site alloying from Na to K
Ab initio calculations of excitonic states, lattice distortion, and radiative pathways
Time-resolved anisotropy measurements to test predicted PL polarization fingerprints
evidence_signal: Experiments and theory show PL shifts from about 2.48 to 2.70 eV while absorption near 3.8 eV stays nearly unchanged, and measured anisotropy matches the predicted composition-dependent STE fingerprints.
watch_item: The strong STE response depends on soft-lattice composition, so device performance may be sensitive to exact alloying, defect levels, and nanocrystal synthesis control.
paper_title: Composition-controlled optical fingerprints and anisotropy of self-trapped excitons in double perovskites
